scope: Bounded public-source claims for the nLDMOS process-sequence review. Patent examples do not establish prevalence or a foundry recipe.

US7405117.title: Method of fabricating a lateral double-diffused MOSFET (LDMOS) transistor
US7405117.access_note: Full description and claims opened on Google Patents; direct USPTO full-text access is not claimed.

EP1119050.title: BiCDMOS process technology and structures
EP1119050.access_note: Full 60-page PDF opened from the European Patent Office publication server.

HOWER2005.title: Short and Long-Term Safe Operating Area Considerations in LDMOS Transistors
HOWER2005.access_note: Six-page paper text opened from a public mirror. Publisher-hosted access was not verified.

MIT720J_L30.title: Lecture 30: The Short MOSFET
MIT720J_L30.access_note: Full 21-page official MIT OpenCourseWare lecture PDF opened.

claims.claim: In the US patent's process 600, the Fig. 7 example uses a p-type substrate with an HV n-well and describes a non-self-aligned P-body implant before LDMOS gate oxide formation.

evidence.locator: Process 600, steps 602-608 and Figs. 7A-7D; description lines 681-685 in Google Patents text.
Step 610 and Fig. 7E; description lines 688-692 in Google Patents text.

claims.technical_limit: This establishes the patent's named example only. Process 600 does not describe an N+ buried layer or epitaxial layer in this illustrated slice; that absence must not be generalized to all nLDMOS devices or all embodiments in the patent.
claims.uncertainty: Production prevalence and present-day foundry usage are unknown.

claims.claim: In EP 1 119 050 A1's illustrated BiCDMOS flow, patterned poly gate precedes the DMOS P-body implant, which the description identifies as self-aligned to the poly gate; body drive follows.

evidence.locator: Table 1, steps 49-54, PDF p. 4; paragraphs [0051]-[0055], PDF pp. 8-9.

claims.technical_limit: Paragraph [0020] explicitly allows listed steps to be eliminated, reversed, or combined in some embodiments. This is not a universal sequence requirement.
claims.uncertainty: Prevalence across BCD platforms and current production flows is unknown.

claims.claim: EP 1 119 050 A1 Table 1 places N+ and P+ buried-layer formation, epi growth, P+ isolation, and N+ sinker formation before its gate/poly module.

evidence.locator: Table 1, steps 1-20 and 42-54, PDF pp. 4-5; [0020] qualification on PDF p. 5.

claims.technical_limit: This describes a BiCDMOS platform sequence and its table qualification, not a required module set for every BCD implementation.
claims.confidence: high for the table as printed
claims.uncertainty: The patent does not quantify how representative this platform is of other processes.

claims.claim: Neither cited patent supports the claim that n+ source/drain implantation before gate geometry is universally impossible; the sources describe different flow choices and US 7,405,117 B2 explicitly permits its shallow N-LD implant before or after gate formation.

evidence.locator: Process 600, step 614, description lines 695-697; n+ and p+ implants are step 616, lines 698-700.
[0058]-[0061], PDF pp. 9-10, describes later N+ and P+ S/D implants for its illustrated sequence.

claims.technical_limit: The US patent's explicit before/after option concerns the shallow N-LD implant, not a blanket permission for every n+ S/D module. Keep these implant categories distinct. Neither source establishes a universal ordering rule.
claims.uncertainty: Whether a particular early n+ S/D step is compatible depends on the specific process integration and device design; the sources do not resolve an unspecified preset.

claims.claim: US 7,405,117 B2 describes a two-implant P-body implementation and associates implant/drive choices with depth, lateral diffusion, channel length, and threshold control.

evidence.locator: Figs. 8A-8C and description lines 685-689; two-implant details are introduced as 'one implementation'.

claims.technical_limit: These are qualitative descriptions of one implementation. They do not supply portable implant/anneal values or predict profiles without process-specific models and measurements.
claims.confidence: high for what the patent says
claims.uncertainty: Transferability to another technology is unsupported.

claims.claim: The EP patent's device structures illustrate P+ body-contact topology as embodiment dependent: one structure can connect the body contact through a P sinker/buried layer, while another confines the P+ contact to the P-body.

evidence.locator: [0095]-[0100], PDF pp. 14-15; especially [0099]-[0100] for the contrasting Figure 25 and Figure 26 structures.

claims.technical_limit: The structural embodiments establish a useful body-contact example but do not prescribe one universal tie layout.
claims.uncertainty: Other process/device architectures may use different body-tie geometries.

claims.claim: A single Rsp-versus-breakdown comparison is not a complete LDMOS safe-operating-area view; the cited paper frames design as also involving short-term and long-term SOA.

evidence.locator: Full paper, SOA regimes PDF pp. 1-2 and conclusion PDF p. 6; public mirror copy.

claims.technical_limit: The paper gives a context-specific design/characterization framing, not a universal qualification limit or lifetime model.
claims.uncertainty: Quantitative limits require device-, package-, application-, and stress-specific evidence.

claims.claim: MIT OCW Lecture 30 supports the general MOSFET physics statement that short-channel inversion-layer devices can show mobility degradation and velocity saturation that reduce current relative to simple long-channel models.

evidence.locator: Full lecture PDF pp. 3-4 and 10-14; summary on p. 21.

claims.technical_limit: The lecture is not LDMOS-specific and does not support P-body diffusion, implant chronology, drift design, or foundry process claims.
claims.confidence: high for the lecture's stated general MOSFET physics
claims.uncertainty: Any application to a specific LDMOS operating regime requires device-specific analysis.
